purpose: Clascoterone is a cream used to treat acne on the face and body in people 12 years and older. It helps reduce pimples, blackheads, and skin blemishes caused by acne. It is one of the few acne treatments that works by blocking hormones right at the skin level.
how_it_works: Your skin has receptors that respond to male hormones called androgens, and when these hormones attach to those receptors, they can cause your oil glands to produce too much oil, leading to acne. Clascoterone works by blocking those hormone receptors in the skin, so the hormones cannot trigger excess oil production. Less oil means fewer clogged pores and less acne over time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are local skin reactions where you apply the cream, such as redness, dryness, skin peeling, stinging or burning, and itching. These are usually mild and tend to get better as your skin adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not use this cream near your eyes, mouth, or on areas with broken or irritated skin. Since clascoterone blocks hormones, there is a small chance it could affect hormone levels in your body, especially with long-term or widespread use, so use only the amount your doctor prescribes. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medication. Keep it away from children and do not use more than directed.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer of the 1% cream to the affected area twice a day, in the morning and at night. Wash your hands before and after applying. Use it consistently every day for best results, and it may take several weeks before you notice a significant improvement in your acne.
